quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a rider become more visible?

options.text: Using a headlight at all times

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake light correctly. Waving does not help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead. Speeding up can make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do to become more visible on the road?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing. Keep your headlight on at all times. Change your lane position as needed for safety.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They allow you to see everything you need to see.
You don't have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They allow you to see everything you need to see.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision in an unsafe way. They allow you to see everything needed for safe riding.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of your tire sidewalls. You do not need to check how reflective your tires are.

questions.question: A driver on an entrance ramp may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a different lane, away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane, away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can. If you can't change lanes, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what rule applies?

options.text: You can pass in a no passing zone.
You can travel 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You must pass on the shoulder if one is available.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and complete a pass only in areas where passing is safe and legal. Stay at or below the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is OPEN, not closed.

questions.question: When a vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes safely and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up makes things more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you travel?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
At the same speed you would travel during the day under the same conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under the same conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat. Why?

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if you need to.
So your legs can absorb the impact.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the force from the bump. This keeps the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slower body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both physical and mental functions.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help reduce crash risk?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible and signal what you plan to do. Stay alert and be ready to react to hazards. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you remember when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane throughout the curve.
Always stay in the left part of the lane throughout the curve.
Always stay in the right part of the lane throughout the curve.
The best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not follow the road's curve.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should less experienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them.

questions.question: What is the best group formation for curves, turns, and entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally best for group riding, switch to single-file for curves, turns, and when entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: How can you discourage other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop other drivers from trying to squeeze in beside you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Hold the grips tight and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: The weaving from rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Spot hazards and decide which ones to handle first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide the order to handle them. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Get in the habit of using both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes in a quick stop is easier if you practice this habit every time.

questions.question: Good motorcycle riders know they are safest when they are:

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good riders know they are safest when other drivers can see them clearly. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injuries, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: When your rear tire skids:

options.text: It is only a problem if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot steer your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the wheel. Once the rear wheel locks, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loosely in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect handling. Put weight toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and beside you. A properly adjusted mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but seeing the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of the braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
Should not be used unless the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.
